title: Constrain autonomous USB-C sources to rails they physically possess
problem: A generic programmable PD source can advertise unsafe voltages or currents that its input, conversion, stackup and thermal path cannot provide.
rootCause: PDO policy and dense-controller breakout were not structurally bound to input-rail capability, protected source-switch limits, configuration firmware, required bulk capacitance and a KiCad-proven copper stackup.
solution: Board005 accepts only regulated SELV 5V/2A input and advertises one 5V/1.5A PDO through a TPS25750 integrated protected source path. The EEPROM image is immutable evidence; fuse, TVS, discharge, bulk capacitance and thermal-via requirements are mandatory. Its six-layer stack isolates GND, DRAIN, VBUS, PP5V and 3V3 rail merges after F.Cu courtyard escape and is enforced because the exact serialized breakout passed KiCad CLI DRC with zero violations.
limitations: No 9V/15V/20V PDO, battery, boost stage or mains input is supported.
The TI configuration image and thermal behavior require proof before manufacturing.
Four-layer parity is not claimed; any reduced-layer allocator requires a separate zero-violation KiCad integration proof.
